meta.engine: LanceDB 0.40.0 (lancedb python package; Rust lance engine)
meta.maintenance_api_call: table.optimize()  # defaults: cleanup_older_than=7d, delete_unverified=False, retrain deprecated
meta.maintenance_semantics: LanceDB's VACUUM-like path: compacts fragments AND rewrites the vector index. Observed: index_uuid and created_at change, size_bytes changes, rows stay 20000. No vector is deleted.

index_types.hnsw: lancedb.index.HnswFlat(distance_type='l2', num_partitions=16, m=20, ef_construction=150); engine reports it as IvfHnswFlat
index_types.ivfpq: lancedb.index.IvfPq(distance_type='l2', num_partitions=16, num_sub_vectors=16); engine reports it as IvfPq

protocol.exact_reference: numpy full pairwise L2, argsort top-10
protocol.episode: top10(genA, q) vs top10(genB, q); genA = after create_index, genB = after table.optimize()
protocol.tear_def: set(top10_before) != set(top10_after)  (ANY-DIFFERENCE convention: these engines expose no HNSW adjacency, so a structural tear cannot be certified)
protocol.cells_per_seed_index: default + same-generation controls (A and B) + recall-matched R in {0.90,0.95,0.99}

deviations: LanceDB exposes no HNSW adjacency -> the paper's structural-tear (A5) claim is NOT certified here; only the answer-level (A4) any-difference tear is measured.

Data is inserted as 8 appends (fragments) and the index is built over those fragments, then table.optimize() compacts them; the same tear also appears with 1 fragment, so the effect is the index rewrite, not compaction per se.
The engine's default search (no explicit knob) is used for the headline cell; the recall-matched cell adjusts the engine's own effort knob.
Uniform random data as in the paper's engine experiment; no vector is removed by optimize().
limitations: Second engine is LanceDB (embedded library-backed system), not a server-side multi-tenant vector DB; it ships its own on-disk index + compaction path.
Recall-matched control is at R in {0.90,0.95,0.99}; the tear is reported at each.

addendum_compaction_only_and_anchored.compaction_only: table.compact_files() merges the 8 fragments into 1 and rewrites the index file (new index_uuid) but the graph is remapped faithfully -> tear 0.000 in all 3 seeds. The tear therefore comes from table.optimize()'s index-rebuild/re-optimize step, not from file compaction per se.
addendum_compaction_only_and_anchored.anchored_recallmatch: gen A is searched with the engine's DEFAULT settings (its native recall); gen B is searched at the ef whose recall best matches it. Controls the 'generation B is simply a worse index' objection.
